What this shows: Operational health of an XRPL node: sync state, ledger progress, caches, storage, job queue, and network economy.
Use it to: Get an at-a-glance read on whether the node is healthy, synced, and keeping up with the network.

panels.title: Validated Ledger Age
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How old the most recently validated ledger is, in seconds.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of the validated-ledger-age gauge, refreshed each collection interval.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; it should stay near the network close interval.*

###### Healthy range:
*Under about 7 seconds on a healthy node.*

###### Watch for:
*Values above 20 seconds mean the node is falling behind the network.*

###### Source:
[LedgerMaster.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/ledger/LedgerMaster.h)

###### Function:
`LedgerMaster::Stats::collectMetrics`

panels.title: Operating Mode (Time Share)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Fraction of recent wall-clock time the node spent in each operating mode (Disconnected, Connected, Syncing, Tracking, Full).*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of each per-mode duration counter divided by the sum of all five mode rates, giving each mode's time share.*

###### Reading it:
*The Full share should sit at or near 1.0 and dominate; other shares should be near 0.*

###### Healthy range:
*Full share close to 1.0.*

###### Watch for:
*Share accumulating in Syncing, Connected, or Disconnected means the node is not staying fully synced.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

###### Function:
`NetworkOPsImp::Stats`

panels.title: Operating Mode Transitions
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Cumulative count of transitions into each operating mode.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of each per-mode transition counter, plotted as lines.*

###### Reading it:
*Flat lines are healthy; steps up mean the node changed mode.*

###### Healthy range:
*Few transitions once the node is stable in Full mode.*

###### Watch for:
*Frequent transitions out of Full, or into Disconnected or Syncing, indicate instability.*

[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

panels.title: I/O Latency
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Latency of the I/O service loop, at the 95th percentile in milliseconds.*

###### How it's computed:
*I/O loop latency samples aggregated to their 95th percentile per node over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; it reflects how promptly queued I/O work runs.*

###### Healthy range:
*A few milliseconds; brief spikes are tolerable.*

###### Watch for:
*Sustained values above a few hundred ms indicate thread-pool saturation or blocking operations.*

###### Source:
[Application.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/main/Application.cpp)

###### Function:
`ApplicationImp`

panels.title: Job Queue Depth
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Number of jobs currently waiting in the internal work queue.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of the job-count gauge, plotted over time.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; a near-flat low line means the node keeps up with its workload.*

###### Healthy range:
*Low single digits at idle, brief bumps under load.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained high depth means the node cannot process work fast enough, common during replay, heavy RPC, or a request flood.*

###### Source:
[JobQueue.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/core/detail/JobQueue.cpp)

panels.title: Ledger Fetch Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often the node requests a ledger from its peers.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of ledger-fetch requests over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*Near zero in steady state; elevated while catching up.*

###### Healthy range:
*Close to zero once fully synced.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained high rate means the node is repeatedly missing ledgers and back-filling from peers.*

###### Source:
[InboundLedgers.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/ledger/detail/InboundLedgers.cpp)

###### Healthy range:
*Zero.*

###### Watch for:
*Any nonzero value indicates consensus divergence or database corruption and warrants immediate investigation.*

###### What this is:
*Cumulative count of peers disconnected for exceeding resource limits.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of the resource-disconnect gauge, plotted over time.*

###### Reading it:
*A flat line is healthy; steps up mean peers were dropped for overuse.*

###### Healthy range:
*Flat or very slowly rising.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising line indicates peers are being throttled off, consistent with abusive or misbehaving peers.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerServerInfoGauge`

panels.title: Base Fee (drops)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The node's local load-based fee factor that scales its minimum transaction cost; baseline 256 at idle.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of the local load-fee economy gauge.*

###### Reading it:
*Steady at the baseline (256) is normal; higher values mean the node is raising its fee in response to load.*

###### Healthy range:
*Around 256 (the normal baseline) when idle.*

###### Watch for:
*A climbing factor, which indicates the node is under transaction load pressure.*

[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

panels.title: Ledger Age
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Seconds since the last validated ledger closed, plotted over time.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of the ledger-age economy gauge, sampled each interval.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; it should stay near the ledger close interval. Mirrors the Validated Ledger Age panel.*

###### Healthy range:
*Under about 10 seconds.*

###### Watch for:
*Growth beyond the expected close interval, meaning the node is not keeping up with validated ledgers.*

panels.title: FullBelowCache Size
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Number of entries in the FullBelowCache, which tracks subtrees known to be fully present locally.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of the cache size gauge, plotted over time.*

###### Reading it:
*A stable size is normal; it grows during acquisition and is trimmed by sweeps.*

###### Healthy range:
*Stable within its configured bound.*

###### Watch for:
*Unbounded growth suggests the cache is not being swept.*

###### Source:
[TaggedCache.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/include/xrpl/basics/TaggedCache.h)

###### Function:

panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Hit-rate percentage for the FullBelowCache.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of the cache hit-rate gauge.*

###### Reading it:
*Higher is better; it shows how often cached subtree knowledge is reused.*

###### Healthy range:
*Above roughly 50 percent in steady state.*

###### Watch for:
*A low hit rate during steady state means redundant subtree work and warrants investigation.*

panels.title: Ledger Publish Gap
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The lag between published and validated ledger ages, in seconds.*

###### How it's computed:
*Published ledger age minus validated ledger age, as a single derived value.*

###### Reading it:
*Near zero is healthy; a positive value is how far publishing trails validation.*

###### Healthy range:
*Close to zero.*

###### Watch for:
*A growing gap means the publish pipeline is falling behind and subscribers may see stale data.*

[LedgerMaster.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/ledger/LedgerMaster.h)

panels.title: State Duration Rate (Full vs Tracking)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of change of time spent in Full and Tracking modes, normalized to seconds per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of the Full and Tracking duration counters, scaled to seconds.*

###### Reading it:
*The Full line near 1.0 means the node gains a second of Full-mode time each wall-clock second.*

###### Healthy range:
*Full rate close to 1.0, Tracking near 0.*

###### Watch for:
*A Full rate below 1.0 means the node is spending time in other modes.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; populated mainly during sync or back-fill.*

*Low when synced; higher and more active while catching up.*

panels.title: Operating Mode (State Timeline)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The node's operating mode over time as a colored timeline (Disconnected, Connected, Syncing, Tracking, Full).*

###### How it's computed:
*Current value of the server-state gauge mapped to a mode name; equal consecutive samples are merged into a single band.*

###### Reading it:
*A solid green Full band across the window is the goal; other colors mark periods the node was not fully synced.*

###### Healthy range:
*Continuously Full (green).*

###### Watch for:
*Bands of Syncing, Connected, or Disconnected, which pinpoint exactly when the node dropped out of Full.*

panels.title: % Time in Full
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The share of recent wall-clock time the node spent in Full mode.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of the Full-mode duration counter divided by the sum of the per-second rates of all five mode duration counters.*

###### Reading it:
*Higher is better; 1.0 means the node was fully synced for the entire window.*

###### Healthy range:
*At or above 0.99.*

###### Watch for:
*Values dropping below 0.9, meaning the node spent meaningful time outside Full mode.*
